articles.title: Diwali rush, GRAP curbs bring Delhi to a crawl: Long jams, illegal parking leave commuters fuming
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi witnessed long queues of vehicles, gridlocked market roads and slow-moving traffic on Wednesday as festive shopping, traffic congestion
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi witnessed long queues of vehicles, gridlocked market roads and slow-moving traffic on Wednesday as festive shopping, traffic congestion and restrictions under GRAP added to commuters' woes.From the narrow, crowded lanes of Sadar Bazar and Karol Bagh to major intersections across central Delhi, commuters reported prolonged traffic jams and encroachments that left little space for pedestrians. Several also complained of inadequate traffic personnel at key congestion points.At Sadar Bazar, the stretch towards Qutub Road Chowk witnessed severe congestion, with two-wheelers and other vehicles allegedly parked illegally along the footpath, leaving pedestrians with almost no space to walk. Commuters also pointed to the absence of cranes to tow unauthorisedly parked vehicles and clear the encroachments.Similar scenes were reported on Ajmal Khan Road, where commuters complained of indiscriminate parking and alleged that authorities had failed to act despite the problem recurring daily.According to news agency PTI, the festive shopping rush ahead of Diwali further strained already congested roads, with commuters reporting slow-moving traffic and long queues at several busy intersections.Traffic snarls were reported at multiple locations across central and north Delhi, including Inderlok, where vehicles reportedly remained almost stationary at a traffic signal for nearly 30 minutes.Motorists on Teen Murti Marg and Kushak Road said they were stuck in traffic for around 20 minutes, while heavy congestion was also reported on the stretch from 11 Murti towards Dhaula Kuan.The stretch from Tal Katora Road towards Shankar Road was reported to be heavily congested, with commuters seeking intervention from traffic personnel. Similar complaints emerged from the area around the Blind School, where a Diwali mela was underway. Commuters said traffic had slowed to a crawl, with long queues building up on adjoining roads.At Modi Mill near Kalkaji, motorists reported more than 200 cars stuck in traffic for over 30 minutes, claiming that the congestion had become a daily occurrence, particularly during peak hours. Traffic snarls were also reported at Dwarka and East of Kailash.Further north, commuters reported severe congestion at Prerna Chowk near Keshav Puram and on the road outside Keshav Puram Metro station, alleging that stationary and improperly parked vehicles were adding to the bottlenecks.Traffic was also moving at a snail's pace at Azadpur Flyover, while motorists flagged rampant wrong-side driving and other traffic violations.In south Delhi, motorists flagged congestion outside Vasant Kunj police station, attributing it to a large number of vehicles parked outside the premises and a nearby traffic signal that allegedly compounded the bottleneck.Complaints also emerged from Jasola, where commuters alleged that unauthorised parking had taken over stretches of the road, with traffic police personnel reportedly attributing the parking arrangements to permissions granted by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi.At the Ghazipur border, the enforcement of restrictions on non-BS-VI vehicles entering Delhi added another layer to the traffic situation.Vehicles entering from Uttar Pradesh were being checked by personnel, with traffic police identifying vehicles through their registration series and other vehicle details to ascertain their registration year and emission standard.Visuals shared online showed vehicles navigating through severely congested stretches near Akshardham Temple amid dense fog and reduced visibility. Commuters also flagged traffic congestion at Inderlok, Pitampura, Keshav Puram and several other locations, seeking immediate intervention from the Delhi Traffic Police.Commuters also called for the deployment of additional traffic personnel and volunteers at major intersections, saying inadequate staffing and indiscriminate parking were adding to congestion during the festive rush.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Florida woman Amanda Brown allegedly impersonated the families of three murdered men to collect more than $11,000 through fake GoFundMe pages
articles.summary: A fundraising page created in the aftermath of a triple murder in Florida was meant to provide financial support to three grieving families.
articles.body: A fundraising page created in the aftermath of a triple murder in Florida was meant to provide financial support to three grieving families. Instead, the donations became the subject of a police investigation after relatives discovered that someone had been collecting money using their names and photographs without their knowledge. Amanda Brown, a 32-year-old Florida woman, was accused of setting up a fraudulent GoFundMe campaign and taking nearly $12,000 from people who believed they were helping the victims' relatives. The investigation eventually traced the money to a series of purchases, cash withdrawals and household payments, leading to Brown's arrest in September 2020.Florida triple murder sparks unauthorised fundraising campaignAs reported by the WFLA, the case began with the deaths of Brandon Rollins, Damion Tillman and Keven Springfield, who were killed on July 17, 2020, near Lake Streety in Frostproof, Polk County, Florida. The three men, aged 27, 23 and 30 respectively, had gone fishing when they were attacked. Their deaths prompted an investigation and left their families facing the practical and emotional consequences of losing relatives in a violent crime.The killings attracted attention in the local community, and the victims' relatives became the focus of public concern. As news of the deaths spread, people were willing to contribute towards helping the families. Online fundraising offered a straightforward way for supporters, including those outside Florida, to send financial assistance.Fake GoFundMe campaign allegedly raises nearly $12,000Amanda Brown was accused of creating a GoFundMe page that presented itself as a way to raise money for the relatives of the three murdered men. According to reports, “The booking photographs of the subject was reviewed at which time, I noticed the subject seen on the surveillance images resemble Amanda Brown.”The deception came to light when relatives noticed the unfamiliar fundraising page. “She used my name, used my son’s picture to gather money that these people thought they were giving to my family,” Dottie Payton, the mother of victim Brandon Rollins.Payton said she had not given permission for her identity or her son's image to be used in this way. The discovery raised concerns about where the donations were going and whether the money had reached any of the people it was supposed to help.The amount involved was reported to be close to $12,000. People who had contributed believed they were supporting families dealing with the aftermath of a triple homicide, while investigators were examining allegations that the money had instead been diverted for Brown's personal use.Investigation traces GoFundMe donations to Walmart and ATM withdrawalsThe investigation led deputies to examine how the collected money had been spent. According to Polk County authorities, surveillance footage showed Brown making transactions at different locations around the county, including Walmart and several ATM machines.Steve Lester, then a chief with the Polk County Sheriff's Office, described the spending activity in an interview with WFLA. Among the payments investigators identified was a $1,300 water bill in Frostproof. Authorities said the donations had been used for personal purchases and expenses rather than being passed on to the victims' relatives.The transactions helped investigators build a picture of how the money had been handled after it was collected. As reported by The New York Post, surveillance images also became important in identifying the person suspected of operating the fraudulent fundraising page.For the families, the investigation brought a separate concern to an already difficult period. Their loss had prompted strangers to offer financial support, but the unauthorised appeal meant that donations made in good faith were allegedly being used by someone with no connection to the intended beneficiaries.Amanda Brown arrested over alleged GoFundMe donation fraudBrown was arrested on September 20, 2020, according to the September 28 report by The New York Post. She was 32 at the time and faced allegations involving fraud, grand theft and the unauthorised use of the identity of a deceased person.Authorities said Brown admitted to the conduct during the investigation. Her identification was also linked to surveillance photographs collected as deputies looked into the false donation campaign.Her arrest reportedly came after she had been detained in connection with separate methamphetamine charges. Investigators examining that matter recognised her in images obtained during the GoFundMe inquiry, according to the local reporting cited at the time.Victims' relatives expressed anger over the alleged deceptionFor Dottie Payton, the discovery was particularly upsetting because her son's identity had been used to attract donations. Speaking to WFLA, she said people had been led to believe they were contributing directly to her family when that was not the case.Payton also voiced her anger towards Brown after the allegations emerged. Her comments reflected the frustration of a relative who had already lost a son and then discovered that his death had allegedly been used as the basis for a fraudulent appeal.Polk County Sheriff's Office Chief Steve Lester also criticised the alleged conduct, describing it as despicable. The investigation highlighted how online fundraising pages can be used to collect money in the aftermath of a tragedy, even when the people named as beneficiaries have no involvement in setting them up.For donors, the case raised questions about checking who controls a fundraising campaign and whether the named beneficiaries have confirmed their involvement. A page carrying a victim's photograph or a relative's name does not, by itself, establish that the family has authorised the appeal.Florida triple murder case remains separate from GoFundMe fraudThe investigation into the deaths of Rollins, Tillman and Springfield proceeded separately. Three people were charged in connection with the killings: brothers Tony, also known as TJ, Wiggins and Robert Wiggins, along with Tony Wiggins' girlfriend, Mary Whittemore.Their arrests were reported in July 2020, shortly after the three men were found dead near Lake Streety. The homicide allegations and the subsequent fundraising investigation involved different individuals and distinct sets of charges.The GoFundMe case centred on money raised in the victims' names, with investigators alleging that Brown had taken nearly $12,000 intended to assist their relatives. The discovery of the unauthorised campaign came from the families themselves, whose concerns prompted police to investigate how the donations had been collected and spent.You use AI every day. articles.title: US midterms 2026: Republicans trumped, stumped, and dumped as Democrats win both House and Senate
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent From Washington: It is a rout of the Republicans, a political bloodbath of epic proportions.
articles.body: TOI Correspondent From Washington: It is a rout of the Republicans, a political bloodbath of epic proportions. Donald Trump may have perfected the art of firing people on television, but on Tuesday night American voters turned the tables, handing him and his MAGA-infused Republican Party an electoral pink slip -- and a political red card -- effectively transitioning the two remaining years of his presidency into a legislative obstacle course.Democrats swept both chambers of Congress, wresting control of the Senate and the House of Representatives in a spectacular voter repudiation of the MAGA boss, his shambolic administration, and policies that have propelled the US into trade wars, shooting wars, and a cost of living crisis on top of racism, bigotry, and xenophobia from the more extreme ranks. Dems also stormed GOP fortresses, capturing governors’ mansions and many local bodies, overturning political assumptions that had survived generations of American elections.The scale of the Democratic victory was quite stunning for the modern era when narrow majorities are the norm. Republicans entered the election with a 53-47 advantage in the Senate and a slim House majority (218-214). Democrats flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats, taking the chamber with a projected 53-41 advantage among contests already called at the time of writing, with the possibility of extending it to 55-45. In the House, Democrats were heading towards 240+ seats, with the slim Republican majority of four seats buried under a Democratic demolition.But it was not simply a change of congressional arithmetic. It was a political map being redrawn in places where Republicans had strutted like they owned the territory, and nowhere was it more apparent than in Texas, a GOP stronghold for almost 40 years.In a result that would have seemed fanciful even a few months ago, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated three-term Republican Governor Greg Abbott, becoming the first Latina governor of a state that was successively a province of Spanish America, a Mexican territory, and an independent sovereign republic before being annexed into the United States. Texas also elected Democrat James Talarico to the Senate, the first Democratic Senator from the state since Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.Similar political convulsions in Maine saw Democrat Troy Jackson defeat Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine, ending her nearly 30-year Senate career that was considered impregnable. South Carolina, a Republican bastion, elected Democrat Annie Andrews to the Senate defeating Darlene Graham, sister of four-term Senator Lindsay Graham. Kansas, which has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932 delivered another stunning upset, sending Adam Hamilton to Washington. Democrats also captured Senate seats in Michigan (Abdul El-Sayed), Ohio (Sherrod Brown) and Iowa (Josh Turek) and New Hampshire, where Chris Pappas became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate.The results were less a blue wave than a political tsunami, sweeping away some of the GOP's most deeply entrenched assumptions that pre-date Trump, who effectively took the party down with him because the shock extended well beyond the Senate. Georgia elected Keisha Lance Bottoms as the first Black woman governor in American history, while Ohio went to Democrat Amy Acton who defeated Indian-American Trump ally Vivek Ramaswamy. Candidates behind whom Trump put his heart, soul, and body, often telling voters to assume he was on the ballot, were sent packing.The rout shocked and angered even conservatives, many of whom began to turn on Trump. “Dems look like they might get 56 (Senate seats).. Rs will never get that back for a long time. You ignore primaries for years, anoint a charlatan as not just leader but God, and then mimic his retardation every day for a decade, at some point the chickens come home to roost,” raged Daniel Horowitz, a commentator at the right leaning outlet The Blaze. "It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told BBC, calling it “a disaster of the first magnitude” that nobody saw coming.Actually, every poll and survey other than MAGA affiliated ones saw it coming, although the scale was not foreseen by most. In fact, Democrats went to polling day wary of the “too good to be true” projections given past setbacks, particularly in 2016 when Trump himself did not appear to believe he would win. This time around, he tried to conjure up victory in the face of imminent defeat, but voters had other ideas.Convulsions were afoot even within the Democratic Party, with radicals and progressives making a mark, most notably in Los Angeles where Democrat Socialist Nithya Raman was leading establishment Democrat Karen Bass by a narrow 16,000 votes in the mayoral election as the time of writing. Washington DC itself elected council member Janeese Lewis George, a Democratic Socialist, as Mayor, an in-your-face repudiation of Trump in the nation’s capital.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital on Wednesday, hours after the veteran leader was discharged earlier in the day.In a social media post on X, Supriya Sule said that her father was admitted for further tests."We are admitting Baba (Sharad Pawar) to Breach Candy Hospital for further tests. articles.title: Kolkata Fire Officials Inspect Kali Puja Pandals, Flag Safety Violations
articles.summary: Kolkata fire and police officials inspected Kali Puja pandals, flagging safety violations at Janbazar Puja; notice planned over height and road stage issues.
articles.body: Kolkata: A high-powered team consisting of the minister of state for fire services, Koushik Choudhury, DG (fire) Anuj Sharma and joint CP (headquarters) Sudeep Sarkar along with multiple fire and police personnel visited at least six major Kali Puja pandals across the city to take stock of the safety protocols being followed at these venues.This was a historic first for Kali Puja, coming just weeks after the Chorbagan stampede that killed 19 persons and injured 25 others. The pandals covered included biggies like Amherst Street, Janbazar and Sarsuna. The team also studied the entry and exit plans at important Kali temples like Kalighat and Karunamoyee.The team pointed to some gross violations at Janbazar Puja, now in its 56th year. It has been reported that the pandal was built without complying with height regulations. Questions have also been raised over cultural events being held on a stage constructed on the road by partially blocking it. The fire department has objected to these issues and said that a notice will be issued to the committee.“We have found the pandal’s height on the S N Banerjee Road side too high, exceeding standard safety regulations. We also found discrepancies in the stage located near the pandal on a road, which could disrupt traffic flow,” Choudhury said. DG Sharma said the dept asked the organisers to take necessary corrective steps.The Janbazar puja organisers said that they have not yet received any notice. They added that they would review the matter once they get it. Puja committee official Sandipan Saha, Entally MLA from the TMC’s Ritabrata Banerjee camp (Democratic Trinamool Congress), said the puja in Janbazar had been held in the same manner for years, and no irregularities had been found in the past. “The stage for cultural programmes has traditionally been set up on the side of the road without disrupting traffic flow. articles.title: SIR: 26.22 lakh cases pending in state, 88.1% disposed of
articles.summary: Jharkhand SIR: 1.94 crore electoral roll cases disposed (88.1%), 26.22 lakh pending; Chakradharpur completes all categories; final roll due Nov 30.
articles.body: Ranchi: Around 1.94 crore (88.1%) of the cases generated during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls have been disposed of, but 26,22,659 cases remain pending in three categories, chief electoral officer K Ravi Kumar said on Wednesday.Of the 2.21 crore cases under the no-mapping, logical discrepancy and other categories, 1.94 crore had been disposed of and updated on ECINET platform till Wednesday.The biggest backlog is in the logical discrepancy category, where 14,88,802 of the 45,49,961 cases remain pending despite a disposal rate of 67.28%. In no-mapping, 7,95,415 of the 14,04,033 cases are yet to be cleared, with disposal at 43.35%. The other category is close to completion, with 97.91% of cases disposed of and 3,38,442 pending.West Singhbhum emerged as the best-performing district in both notice-related categories, clearing 96.16% of no-mapping cases and 99.72% of logical discrepancy ones, Kumar said in a statement.Lohardaga, Deoghar, Ramgarh and Gumla were among the better-performing districts in no-mapping, while Lohardaga, Gumla, Ramgarh and Simdega led in disposal of logical discrepancy cases.Giridih recorded the lowest disposal rate in no-mapping cases at 19.52%, while Pakur was the worst performer in logical discrepancy at 45.88%. Sahibganj, Palamu and Ranchi also remained among the weaker-performing districts in both categories.At the assembly constituency level, Chakradharpur (ST) became the first constituency to complete work in all three categories. It also topped the combined ranking for no-mapping and logical discrepancy cases.Kumar congratulated the district election officer, electoral registration officers, assistant electoral registration officers, booth-level officers and the Chakradharpur team for almost completing disposal of the notices.He directed lagging districts to prepare special action plans, review pendency regularly and expedite hearings.“The exercise must ensure that the name of every eligible Indian citizen is included in the electoral roll while keeping ineligible or foreign citizens out,” Kumar said.The final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on Nov 30.Kumar inspected the fifth BLO-BLA-2 meeting and Chunav Pathshala at eight polling stations in Ramgarh on Wednesday. He directed officials to expedite home-to-roll verification and digitisation of Form 6 work ahead of the Nov 30 deadline.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: UK prime minister says midterm results a call to ‘unite’ on battling cost of living
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, after Democrats’ sweeping election victories Tuesday, said the world now has an opportunity to come together to fight against affordability concerns. “I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all and that’s the cost of living,” Burnham said early Wednesday during…
articles.body:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, after Democrats’ sweeping election victories Tuesday, said the world now has an opportunity to come together to fight against affordability concerns.

“I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all and that’s the cost of living,” Burnham said early Wednesday during an interview . “That has been the issue that I have put front and center in my first three months in Downing Street.”

Democrats secured control of both the House and the Senate for the next term, including flipping GOP-held seats in battleground states like Texas, Michigan, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa.

Recent polls show that the rising cost of living was a top concern for a lot of voters heading into Election Day. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 48 percent of voters ranked affordability as the most important factor in deciding their vote.

A Gallup survey , conducted last month, found nearly half of the respondents marked the economy as an extremely important factor before casting their ballots.

In his remarks, Burnham also noted that global leaders cannot truly address the issue “until the conflict in the Middle East is resolved.”

President Trump late Tuesday acknowledged that the war in Iran l ikely affected the outcome of the midterms.

In connection with the war, Americans have struggled with higher fuel prices . The national average price for a gallon of gas sits at $4.12 as of Wednesday morning, according to AAA . A year ago, the number stood at $3.05.

The British prime minister noted he is “working for de-escalation.”

“We want to see a resolution [and] the Strait of Hormuz fully open again,” he added later, referring to the key waterway through which a fifth of the world’s oil is transported.

Additionally, inflation saw an uptick in September with the annual rating hovering around 3.7 percent, according to the consumer price index . Democrats across the country campaigned on lowering costs.

“I think people want to see the world coming together and focusing on the things that matter to people and that’s what the voters, in my view, are saying in the United States,” Burnham said.

articles.title: What Trump’s midterms setback could mean for Iran, Israel and Ukraine
articles.summary: The US midterm elections could have consequences far beyond the country’s borders. President Donald Trump has spent nearly two years overturning decades of American foreign policy, unsettling allies and adversaries alike. Now, both are watching to see how an electoral setback at home will shape his actions abroad.
articles.body: The US midterm elections could have consequences far beyond the country’s borders. President Donald Trump has spent nearly two years overturning decades of American foreign policy, unsettling allies and adversaries alike. Now, both are watching to see how an electoral setback at home will shape his actions abroad. For Iran, Israel and Ukraine, the stakes go well beyond who controls Congress. The result could influence whether Trump pursues a deal with Tehran or more war, how much Washington’s longstanding support for Israel erodes, and how hard he pushes Kyiv to accept terms to end Russia’s war. Democrats will have new tools to challenge Trump. But he still has considerable freedom to act abroad, leaving world leaders with a question: Will defeat make him more willing to compromise, or more determined to get his way? Here’s how the vote could impact Washington’s most pressing foreign policy concerns: Iran gloats, but gets no guarantee of peace Iran is celebrating Trump’s midterm setback, but it is bracing for what comes next: a possible new US strike or a fresh push for a deal. Trump admitted in a call with Fox News that the war in Iran was partly to blame for the Republicans’ losses but Vice President JD Vance was more explicit, saying in a lengthy X post Wednesday that “the reason we lost is the war.” After eight months of striking the region’s economic lifelines to turn American voters against the war, Tehran has hailed the Republican loss as a public verdict on it. Trump acknowledged that war-driven price hikes played a role. “If the US government betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare,” parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has led negotiations with the US, wrote on X. Tehran is not betting on a change of course in Washington. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said anyone who believes the results will shift US policy is “deeply mistaken,” and officials say Iran’s strategy doesn’t hinge on American elections as they prepare for more war while intensifying diplomacy. The risk of escalation is real. Reports that Trump might order new, more intense strikes are fueling anxiety across the region, and Tehran has warned that its retaliation would be much wider in scope than in earlier rounds. This week, Trump told some journalists he is considering striking Iran hard, and others that he has no immediate plans to escalate. “The Iran war has become a political albatross around his neck, leaving (Trump) with a stark choice: cut a face-saving deal and declare victory, or double down militarily to reclaim the initiative,” Ali Vaez of International Crisis Group told CNN. “The danger is that a president weakened at the ballot box may seek redemption on the battlefield.” Diplomacy offers another path. Talks that stagnated over the summer have picked up in the past week, with Tehran sending officials to Qatari mediators who are circulating proposals with Washington. Before the vote, Iran offered to open the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Trump agreed to its seven conditions. Sanam Vakil of Chatham House said Iran’s leadership “might feel vindicated,” but that “does not necessarily solve their problems.” Trump needs a diplomatic victory yet may be reluctant to appear weak, she said, while Tehran could read his setback as a chance to demand greater concessions. She expects intensified diplomacy alongside military threats, with an interim Strait of Hormuz deal “more realistic” than a comprehensive one. ‘End of an era’ for US-Israel relations In Israel, the election day announcement that Trump would abruptly cut off US military aid to the country was the first surprise. The results, with Democrats sweeping both chambers of Congress in what has been called a “blue tsunami,” are a five-alarm fire in Israel. Bipartisan support for Israel in the US had already been eroding, with Democrats outraged at Israel over the death toll in the Gaza war and a growing number of Republicans believing the US has given it too much support. “The only bipartisan issue right now is criticism of Israel,” said Michael Oren, a former Israeli ambassador to the US. “It’s an organizing principle for the Democratic Party,” he told CNN. “And it’s becoming an organizing principle for much of the Republican Party.” Oren said the end of US aid is just the beginning of a process that has only started to play out. He said it’s conceivable that the US could end intelligence sharing with Israel and the joint development of critical military systems, such as the vaunted Iron Dome aerial defense system. He also pointed to the United Nations Security Council, where Republican and Democratic presidents have protected Israel with the US veto. “We are at the end of an era,” he said. Yaakov Katz, a former editor-in-chief of the Jerusalem Post, warned there is more to come. “What Trump announced about the military aid yesterday is just the tip of the iceberg of what can change – arms sales could be blocked, sanctions will be proposed and joint economic programs defunded,” he said on X. The anti-Israel sentiment only hardened during the Iran war, with segments of the US electorate viewing the joint US-Israel strikes as a war that Netanyahu sold to Trump. Even now, Netanyahu has been pushing to resume strikes on Iran, which would reignite a war that drove gas prices and the cost of living higher and contributed to Republicans’ devastating midterm performance. Netanyahu also faces turmoil at home. In elections a week before the midterms, he lost his majority in parliament, but his main rival, former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, does not have an outright majority and would likely need to cooperate with Arab parties, who saw record turnout. Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats party, warned that Israel “does not have time to waste” in replacing Netanyahu and leading the country away from sanctions and isolation. Ukraine waits for a post-Trump world For Kyiv, the reaction came before the election. And on Wednesday there was relative silence. For weeks, President Volodymyr Zelensky’s relationship with Trump has been in freefall. Trump has demanded Zelensky be replaced; courted energy deals to benefit Russia; and watched as Ukraine’s tech and intel dependencies on the US were inexplicably thwarted. And so Kyiv was forced to take a position early: wait, with urgency, for a post-Trump world. And when it began to dawn on Wednesday, there was little official comment from Kyiv, Zelensky perhaps happy for the memes of him, sat with a beer and popcorn in front of the mid-term TV coverage, to do the job for him. A deputy in his office, Sergiy Kyslytsia, pledged on Ukrainian TV that the country would continue to “develop genuine, normal and stable relations” with whoever is in office, seek Patriot interceptors, and navigate both a new Congress and the likely flurry of executive orders that may try to obviate it. But there can be no disguising that a crestfallen Trump, and the slow clock now loudly ticking on his worldview and presidency, is in Kyiv’s favour. He had claimed a peace was easy to fashion, yet proceeded to punish Ukraine for not agreeing to the demands of its invader. He humiliated, scolded, and then occasionally made up with, Zelensky, while massaged by European allies, aghast at the breakdown in decades of security alliances. There is still a lot that Ukraine needs Trump and the United States to do. Provide arms, money, and a wider assurance it is on their side. But Kyiv has calculated it cannot depend on Washington, after months of hostility. There is one downside of the ticking clock however: that Russian President Vladimir Putin determines he has likely a year to pursue, at any cost, the best outcome possible in his war of choice, before the 2028 fight drags Republican policy back to the pro-Ukrainian mainstream. Putin has so far failed to use his apparent great ally, Trump, to secure a battlefield win of note. He may seek to change that while the embers of Trump’s authority burn.

articles.title: These Democrats are set to take foreign policy reins in Congress
articles.summary: Correction: An earlier version of this article contained incorrect information about the likely chair of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs. Tuesday’s seismic midterm results hand Democrats significant powers to investigate the Trump administration’s world dealings and check the president’s intervention abroad. The Democrats likely to move into top posts…
articles.body:
Correction: An earlier version of this article contained incorrect information about the likely chair of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs.

Tuesday’s seismic midterm results hand Democrats significant powers to investigate the Trump administration’s world dealings and check the president’s intervention abroad.

The Democrats likely to move into top posts on the foreign policy panels and appropriations committees are seasoned legislators with deep international experience.

Democrats have slammed President Trump’s attacks on U.S. allies and gutting of American soft power tools like foreign aid, government-funded media, and the foreign service itself.

The economic costs of Trump’s war against Iran and tariff policies were top of mind for Americans at the polls, making them top targets for Democrats in Congress. The future U.S. relationship with Israel is a divisive issue on both sides of the aisle and could be shaped in part by the results of Israel’s postelection power struggles.

The next two years serve as an important period for Democrats to sharpen their foreign policy message heading into the 2028 presidential election.

Likely chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee

Sen. Chris Coons, 63, is the leading contender for chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, moving up in the ranks with the retirement of the ranking member, Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.).

Coons, who won reelection in Delaware on Tuesday for his third term, has already telegraphed that going after tech billionaire Elon Musk is a top priority — and the Senate Foreign Relations Committee provides the subpoena power to make that happen.

“One more thing to add to the list of questions for Musk when I subpoena him,” Coons posted on social platform X on Oct. 28, citing a report that the SpaceX owner was in talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin about satellite communications. Musk also owns the social media site X.

Coons is supportive of Ukraine, hawkish on China, outspoken on Israel’s faults but supportive of the Jewish state, and he’s one of the few lawmakers with expertise on the African continent.

He was considered a “shadow” secretary of State during the Biden administration, after being passed over for the top diplomatic role in favor of the president’s close adviser, Antony Blinken.

A former chair of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on State and Foreign Operations, Coons controlled the purse strings for how America funded its foreign policy and where it put its priorities.

Per Democratic caucus rules, Coons will have to be nominated by the Democratic Steering and Outreach Committee and then voted on by the caucus. Seniority is often taken into account.

Chair of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs

The Senate subcommittee is the primary venue for earmarking the State Department’s spending priorities. Sen. Brian Schatz, 54, is the ranking member of the subcommittee but has announced his intention to seek the Democratic whip, the party’s No. 2 in the chamber.

That leaves open who will move into the chair of the Senate subcommittee. The likely remaining members of the subcommittee will be Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), who recently suffered a stroke, and Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.). The rest of the bench is expected to grow from the current six members, and have new faces as Sens. Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) and Shaheen retire.

Still, Schatz has work to do in the remaining weeks of the 119th Congress. Congress faces a Dec. 11 deadline to fund the government for the next year. The Senate has not advanced any spending bills for fiscal 2027, which will make it difficult for Republicans to push through their priorities before handing over majority control in January.

The House has advanced spending bills and Democrats in the lower chamber are looking for a full-year budget so as to start fresh in January.

Likely chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee

Democratic Rep. Gregory Meeks, 73, easily won reelection in New York’s 5th Congressional District. He’s served in Congress since 2013 and was previously chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee between 2021 and 2023. His election to the chairmanship made him the first African American to hold the position.

Meeks served as ranking member of the committee during the 119th Congress under the chairmanship of Republican Rep. Brian Mast (Fla.). Their contentious relationship would frequently spill into public during committee hearings — with Mast a staunch ally of Trump’s America First foreign policy and Meeks pushing back on what he criticized as the president’s destructive actions.

As ranking member of the committee, Meeks blocked arms sales to Israel and successfully discharged legislation to provide more support to Ukraine (a measure that was not taken up in the Senate). Meeks has also introduced legislation to block Trump’s purchase of Russian diesel and introduced a joint resolution of disapproval to block the administration’s pursuit of a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia.

Meeks will have to be nominated by the House Democratic Caucus’s Steering and Policy Committee to serve as chair and then approved by a majority vote of the full caucus.

Likely chair of House Appropriations subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs

Democratic Rep. Lois Frankel, 78, is the new representative for Florida’s 23rd Congressional District after redistricting moved her out of the 22nd District. Frankel is heading into her eighth term in Congress.

She is the ranking member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs.

Frankel will have to bid for the chair of the subcommittee, per House Democratic Caucus rules, and be confirmed through a majority vote, but seniority is generally a primary factor in those appointments.

Frankel signaled she’s looking to chair the subcommittee ahead of reelection, telling FloridaPolitics.com that the position is key to exercising American leadership abroad. Her top issues are humanitarian aid and developmental assistance, as well as strengthening alliances and combatting China’s influence.

“America will be best positioned to compete with China when we invest in our workers and innovation at home while using our diplomatic, humanitarian, and economic strength to lead abroad,” she told the outlet.

She’s also likely to be a champion for women’s and girls’ programs that were gutted by the Trump administration — from contraception assistance to increasing women’s participation in national security and peace negotiations.

articles.title: Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe arrested over 'assault' during Zimbabwe luxury car smuggling probe
articles.summary: The son of Zimbabwe's late former President Robert Mugabe will appear in court on 5 November with four other men.
articles.body:
Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the son of Zimbabwe's late former president Robert Mugabe, has been arrested in connection with an assault case, police say.

He was one of five men arrested on Tuesday during a probe into the alleged smuggling of two luxury vehicles into Zimbabwe, online news site The New Zimbabwe reports.

According to local media reports, the vehicles have been seized by the Zimbabwe Anti-Corruption Commission.

Mugabe, 29, is the youngest son of Robert Mugabe and his second wife, Grace Mugabe. Robert Mugabe, who died in 2019, ruled Zimbabwe for 37 years before being forced from power at the age of 93 in 2017.

Police said Mugabe was arrested alongside Munashe Mubawu, 43, Terrence Johannes Chinyemba, 42, Fredson Peter, 33, and Solomon Pamire, 34.

All five were arrested in connection with a case of assault which happened at the Brompton Guest Lodge in Harare at about 18:30 local time (16:30 GMT) on 3 November, according to a police statement.

They are due to appear in court on 5 November.

articles.title: Bob the poet, meet Bob the priest: Pope Leo receives Bob Dylan at the Vatican
articles.summary: They are two of the world’s best-known Bobs from the US Midwest. Now Pope Leo XIV, whose birth name is Robert Prevost, and Bob Dylan, the legendary musician, have met in the Vatican.
articles.body: They are two of the world’s best-known Bobs from the US Midwest. Now Pope Leo XIV, whose birth name is Robert Prevost, and Bob Dylan, the legendary musician, have met in the Vatican. Leo and Dylan were both seen meeting in the Vatican’s apostolic palace, the pope’s residence, on Wednesday. The pope was wearing his white cassock and Dylan a black coat, black gloves and a black hoodie. The meeting was brokered by Rev. Antonio Spadaro, a Vatican official known for building bridges between the church and wider culture. Spadaro earlier this year arranged a meeting between Pope Leo and Patti Smith. “It was hard not to feel the emotion of being part of an encounter that had a real sense of history about it, with the feeling that, at every step through the Apostolic Palace, absolutely anything could happen!” Spadaro wrote on social media platforms. The 71-year-old Chicago-born pontiff knows Dylan’s repertoire. He quoted an unpublished 1963 Dylan Song, “Go Away You Bomb” in the preface to a book-length collection of his addresses and reflections published in July. The 1963 song was an anti-nuclear protest, while Pope Leo has been a critic of the war in Iran and emphasized the Catholic Church’s opposition to nuclear weapons. Leo is not, however, the first pope that Dylan has met. At a 1997 church event attended by Pope John Paul II in Bologna, Italy, Dylan played some of his songs, including “Blowin’ in the Wind”, “Knockin’ on Heaven’s Door” and “A Hard Rain’s A-Gonna Fall”. John Paul II, taking a famous line from “Blowin’ in the Wind”, said: “You asked me: how many roads must a man walk down before you call him a man? I answer you: one! There is only one road of man and it is Christ, who said: ‘I am the way’.” The meeting was confirmed by the Vatican’s newspaper which said the pope had “received in private audience Mr. Robert Allen Zimmerman,” using Dylan’s birth name.

articles.title: Israel restricting treatment for 1,100 child amputees in Gaza: NGO
articles.summary: Israeli restrictions on travel and medical evacuations prevent children in Gaza from being treated abroad.
articles.body:
Israel is restricting child amputees in Gaza from seeking treatment abroad, a human rights organisation has claimed.

The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor said that Israeli restrictions on travel also include medical evacuations, preventing hundreds of children from seeking specialised treatment abroad.

The monitor reported on Wednesday that 1,134 children in Gaza had undergone limb amputations due to Israeli attacks, but few are receiving the long-term medical care they need.

The World Health Organization said 2,300 amputees – both children and adults – were assessed for treatment between September 2024 and May 2026.

But only 500 – or less than a quarter – received permanent prosthetics .

“Only eight certified prosthetics and orthotics professionals are currently available in Gaza,” the Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor said.

There isn’t enough equipment to manufacture, fit, maintain and adjust prosthetic limbs in the strip, the Geneva-based organisation reported.

“Continued denial of treatment, rehabilitation, and appropriate education risks turning the harm these children face now into lifelong deprivation,” the organisation warned.

“Gaps in medical follow-up and failure to adjust prosthetic limbs as the children grow may cause further complications, chronic pain, and increased difficulty moving.”

Fidaa Ahmad Al-Shaer, 36, told the human rights organisation that her 11-year-old son was paralysed and lost a hand after an Israeli artillery shell landed near him. He needs multiple surgeries abroad and a prosthetic limb but can’t get through the closed crossings.

The organisation accused Israel of war crimes, saying “deliberately inflicting conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction, in whole or in part, are acts listed in Article 2 of the Genocide Convention”.

“The amputation of children’s limbs and the obstruction of their treatment and rehabilitation form part of this pattern,” the group added.

The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor said Israeli restrictions prevented Palestinians from importing the equipment needed to manufacture prosthetic limbs in Gaza. The organisation added that specialised teams require entry permits to the strip to work and train local teams.

articles.title: Zelensky doubts Musk ‘acted alone’ in Ukraine Starlink slowdown
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed doubt that SpaceX CEO Elon Musk could have acted alone in the Starlink slowdown last month, which impacted Ukraine’s military capabilities. “I’m not sure that he [Musk] can do it with Starshield because it’s military. It’s government version,” Zelensky said during an interview with PBS News. “I’m not sure that…
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed doubt that SpaceX CEO Elon Musk could have acted alone in the Starlink slowdown last month, which impacted Ukraine’s military capabilities.

“I’m not sure that he [Musk] can do it with Starshield because it’s military. It’s government version,” Zelensky said during an interview with PBS News . “I’m not sure that he could do it personally alone, without any representatives from American government.”

“But I don’t know who from American side from the government did it, who allowed him. I think it was a dialogue between some people, and in — during this dialogue, the decision was negative for us,” Zelensky added.

The slowdown restricted Ukraine’s access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink, and targeted Starlink-supported Ukrainian military drones, airplanes and helicopters traveling faster than 100 mph.

Musk initially claimed that the choice to restrict the speed or usage of Starshield is made by the U.S. military and, ultimately, the president.

He later alluded to being involved in the decision in a post on social media, writing, “Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week.”

Ukraine has used Starlink’s commercial services since the beginning of its war with Russia. It later added Starshield through SpaceX’s contract with the Pentagon. Musk in his post said Starlink is “critical to the defense of Ukraine.”

Zelensky during his interview also acknowledged that he is “very thankful” for Starlink and said he wanted to speak with Musk after the slowdown incident. He also said if restrictions were to be lifted, Ukraine would use Starshield “in Russia just to find the points where ballistic launchers are.”

Musk argued in his post last month that using the commercial service “for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be.”

Officials from the Trump administration, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, have said earlier that the White House did not have anything to do with the slowdown.

“The bottom line is that that is governed by a private commercial contract as to how their stuff can be used and what speeds they’ll allow it to be used at,” Rubio told reporters in October.

articles.title: Philadelphia 'boycott ride' targeting Jewish businesses draws condemnation from city, state leadership
articles.summary: Jewish organizations called the upcoming Philadelphia boycott ride targeting Jewish-owned businesses near Rittenhouse Square "Jew-Hatred, plain and simple."
articles.body: Jewish organizations called on Philadelphia and Pennsylvania leaders to condemn an upcoming "boycott ride" targeting pro-Israel and "Zionist establishments" in a statement Monday. The organizations Philly Bike On Your Left, Philly Writers Against the War on Gaza, Boycott CookNSolo and Philly Solidarity Calendar shared a flier promoting the bicycle boycott event at Rittenhouse Square on Nov. 8. "Ride around Rittenhouse with us as we show these zio business owners that we see them for the disgusting humans they are," Philly Bike On Your Left wrote on Instagram. ISRAEL, JEWS TARGETED WORLDWIDE AS WELL-FUNDED LEFTIST, ISLAMIST GROUPS JOIN FOR ‘NAKBA 78’ PROTESTS The flier included the names of Philadelphia businesses, including Dizengoff, Huda, Schlesinger’s and Mac Mart, all of which are owned by either Israeli or Jewish Americans. The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) Philadelphia, American Jewish Committee Philadelphia/Southern NJ, Jewish Federation of Greater Philadelphia and StandWithUs released a joint statement condemning the event as "Jew-Hatred, plain and simple" and called on city and state leadership to do the same. "Free speech protects political expression and criticism of Israeli government policies. It does not provide a license for threats, harassment, intimidation, or discrimination. There is a profound difference between criticizing a government and targeting businesses because their owners are Jewish or perceived to be connected to Israel," the statement read. The organizations also remarked that the boycott's scheduled date would occur on the eve of the 88th anniversary of Kristallnacht, a Nazi-organized attack on Jewish homes, synagogues and businesses in Germany and Austria. WEAPONIZING THE CHARGE OF GENOCIDE FUELS AN INCREASINGLY DANGEROUS ANTISEMITISM In a statement to Fox News Digital, Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker's office pointed to remarks shared Tuesday by Philadelphia Commission on Human Relations (PCHR) Executive Director Renee Chenault-Fattah. "The Philadelphia Commission on Human Relations reaffirms its 75-year commitment to fighting racism, antisemitism and, in recent years, Islamophobia. Acts of bigotry, violence and hate cannot be tolerated, and we will never stand by and allow businesses, individuals or jobs to be run out of our city, full stop," the statement read. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro also issued a statement to Fox News Digital condemning the event and assuring Jewish communities that his administration was working with authorities ahead of Sunday. "The Shapiro Administration is aware of this planned protest and the Pennsylvania State Police is engaged with our local partners to ensure the safety and wellbeing of our neighbors in Philadelphia. This bike ride, masquerading as a protest to advance the cause of justice, is nothing more than blatant antisemitism designed to intimidate and drive Jewish businesses out of our communities, and there is no place for that in our Commonwealth," Shapiro spokesperson Rosie Lapowsky said. Ahead of the planned boycott, some of the targeted businesses reported receiving broad support from the public. Mac Mart owner Marti Lieberman told Fox News Digital that while it is "heartbreaking" to have to defend her business, she hoped the attention would shed light on what other small-business owners were facing. OAKLAND COFFEE SHOP ACCUSED OF KICKING OUT JEWISH DAD, 5-YEAR-OLD SON AND SHUTTERS AMID ANTISEMITISM LAWSUITS "We are absolutely feeling the love from this community, and we don’t take a single order, kind message, or person showing up for us for granted," Lieberman said. articles.body: In March 2024, actor and entrepreneur Eva Longoria received $50 million from Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and his wife, Lauren Sanchez Bezos, through their Courage and Civility Award. Two years later, the Desperate Housewives star has a message about philanthropy: you don't have to be rich or famous to make a difference.In an interview with Fortune, Longoria spoke about one of the biggest misconceptions surrounding charitable work, saying that people often associate meaningful impact with the amount of money someone can donate. She believes, however, that even small acts of support can help bring about change.“One of the biggest misconceptions about philanthropy is that impact is tied to wealth or scale, when in reality, impact comes in many forms,” Longoria told the publication. “What I’ve learned is that impact doesn’t come from how much money you have, it comes from how you show up.”Her message comes at a time when large donations from billionaires often dominate conversations about philanthropy. Longoria believes that giving back should not be seen as something only wealthy individuals can afford to do. According to her, mentoring someone, supporting a small business or sharing professional knowledge can also make a meaningful difference.“Mentoring someone, supporting small business, sharing what you know—those things matter because not everyone has access to capital or resources, but anyone can be part of someone else’s support system,” she added. “And I think that’s really what’s missing for a lot of people. They don’t have someone in their corner.”What Eva Longoria did with Jeff Bezos' $50 million awardLongoria and retired US Navy Admiral Bill McRaven received $50 million each in March 2024. The grants were part of the Bezos Courage and Civility Award, launched by Bezos and Sanchez in 2021 to recognise individuals making significant contributions to society. The award allows recipients to direct the funds towards charitable causes of their choice.For Longoria, the recognition was about more than the financial contribution. She said the award represented trust and responsibility and encouraged her to become more intentional and strategic in her advocacy.“Receiving that support was incredibly meaningful, not just because of the scale of the gift, but because it represented trust and responsibility,” she said.The actress explained that the grant had allowed her to continue investing in communities and causes close to her heart, particularly supporting Latina entrepreneurs, expanding access to education and backing organisations working towards change on the ground.“This award has allowed me to continue investing those resources into the communities and causes I care deeply about—supporting Latina entrepreneurs, expanding access to education, and backing organizations that are driving real change on the ground,” she said.Longoria added that the award had helped the Eva Longoria Foundation create long-term impact through transformative giving. Founded in 2012, the foundation works to improve educational and entrepreneurial opportunities for Latinas in the United States.She is also associated with Eva's Heroes, a charity that supports young adults with intellectual special needs.Eva Longoria is mentoring small-business ownersApart from her foundation work, Longoria is also putting her belief in community-level support into practice through a new partnership with Lenovo, under which she is mentoring small-business owners.The actor has built a business portfolio that includes luxury tequila brand Casa Del Sol, media company Hyphenate Media Group and a stake in women's soccer team Angel City FC. She has also made an early investment in the John Wick franchise.Despite her business success and the resources available to her, Longoria believes that people do not need substantial financial means to help someone else succeed. She sees guidance, mentorship and access to opportunities as important forms of giving.From Van Jones to Eva Longoria: The Bezos Courage and Civility AwardBezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos launched the Courage and Civility Award in 2021 for individuals who make significant contributions to society. Previous recipients include CNN commentator and civil rights advocate Van Jones, chef and humanitarian Jose Andres, and country music legend Dolly Parton.Jones and Andres were among the first recipients, each receiving $100 million. Parton received $100 million in 2022, with her philanthropic work including support for research that helped fund Moderna's COVID-19 vaccine development.In 2024, Longoria and McRaven each received $50 million. McRaven, who oversaw the 2011 US military raid that killed al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden, pledged to use his share for educational programmes for future military leaders and children of deceased veterans, as well as mental health support for military personnel.The Giving Pledge, co-founded by Bill Gates, Melinda French Gates and Warren Buffett in 2010, is another initiative encouraging large-scale philanthropy. It asks billionaires to commit at least half of their wealth to charitable causes. However, questions have been raised about how quickly such pledges translate into actual donations.Two years after receiving the $50 million award, Longoria's message is that philanthropy is not measured only by the size of a cheque. While the grant has given her the resources to support causes on a larger scale, she believes anyone can make a difference by offering their time, knowledge and support to someone who needs it.You use AI every day. articles.body: Feelings need clear names for Libra this Thursday. Venus, your ruling planet and the natural significator of love, is still moving backwards through your own sign. It slips into Virgo tomorrow. Old emotions may surface now. So may hurts that were never voiced, or doubts about where a relationship is heading. Shani, retrograde in Pisces in your sixth house, also rules your fifth house of romance. Silence and polite pretending get no credit from Shani. One frank, kind conversation will help your love life more today than any expensive gift.Questions Worth AskingVenus reversing through your first house turns attention inward. You may wonder whether you give more than you get. Or whether you’ve been hiding your own needs just to keep things smooth. Both are fair questions.The Sun and retrograde Mercury sit with Venus. The Sun can make you defensive, and Mercury may twist what you mean to say. Jot your thoughts down first, then say them in plain sentences.Shani Rewards the TruthFor Libra, Shani owns Aquarius, your fifth house of romance and children. Its retrograde looks back over promises made in love. If you agreed to something you didn’t really mean, this is the moment to correct it, gently.Shani’s third aspect falls on Taurus, your eighth house of trust and intimacy. Trust rebuilds slowly when both people speak openly. Its tenth aspect on Sagittarius, your third house, supports clear words over hints and silences.Ekadashi for Vishnu and LakshmiRambha Ekadashi honours Lord Vishnu along with Goddess Lakshmi, whose qualities are closely tied to Venus. Couples may pray together or share a simple fasting meal. The Moon moves through Uttara Phalguni, a nakshatra of commitment, which supports renewing promises.Friends Will Weigh InJupiter and Ketu in Leo, your eleventh house, may bring a friend’s opinion about your relationship.
